metadata.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
metadata.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

metadata.title: A singular minimizer of a uniformly convex Hessian-dependent functional
metadata.abstract: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory à la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

metadata.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
metadata.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $\theta(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{\theta(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

metadata.title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
metadata.abstract: We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[ \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((\Delta g)\log g)\dd. \] Here $\mu$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $\Delta$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

metadata.title: Translation surfaces with logarithmically growing systole
metadata.abstract: We exhibit a sequence of translation surfaces $T_1, T_2,...$ with $T_g$ of genus $g$ and area $g$, such that the systole grows logarithmically with $g$. metadata.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
metadata.abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $\beta_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leq\beta=\beta_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $\beta\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.

metadata.title: Finite time blow-up for the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori
metadata.abstract: We show that the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori of revolution produces a finite time singularity, provided the initial energy is below $12\pi$. Our approach relies on the connection with elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane and a fine analysis of Palais--Smale sequences in the relevant energy regime.

metadata.title: A Universal $8$-Vertex Origami Torus Triangulation
metadata.abstract: An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into $\R^3$. We prove that every flat torus is realized as an $8$-vertex origami torus based on the triangulation with degree sequence $4,6,6,6,6,6,7,7$. This provides an $8$-vertex universal triangulation for origami tori.

metadata.title: Exotic smooth structures on nonorientable 4-manifolds
metadata.abstract: We construct closed nonorientable aspherical 4-manifolds with an arbitrarily large number of distinct smooth structures. This uses the reflection trick of Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian. Our examples become mutually diffeomorphic after either type of stabilization: taking a product with the real line, or taking a connected sum with sufficiently many copies of S^2 x S^2.

metadata.title: Remarks on thin sets in potential theory for sub-Laplacians
metadata.abstract: In contrast to Euclidean cases, we observe that, there are sets in Heisenberg groups that are thin at the origin and block all geodesics from the origin. metadata.title: Hyperkähler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
metadata.abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $\alpha$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $\sigma$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $\pi:\mathscr M\to\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ encodes $(\alpha,\sigma)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in an open dense subset $\Lambda_0\subset\Lambda$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(\alpha,\sigma)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.

metadata.title: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
metadata.abstract: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=\Delta_pF(u)$. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

metadata.title: On the Morse index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we use the technique developed by the first named author in arXiv:2610.07815 to compute the Morse-index of some Riemannian homogeneous fibrations. For the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf fibration, we compute the index and nullity, where the metric on the $\mathbb{S}^7$ (resp. $\mathbb{S}^{15}$) is the quaternionic (resp. octonionic) Hopf--Berger metric. In particular, for the round metric on the domain, the Morse-index is $45$ (resp. $153$). We also give a spectral formula for the Aloff--Wallach projections. In particular, we obtain that the Konishi $\mathbb{R} P^3$-fibration $N_{1,1}\to\mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable throughout the two-parameter metric family, while the unit tangent sphere bundle $T^1(\mathbb{C} P^2)\to \mathbb{C} P^2$ is stable under some conditions on the metric. We also compute the index and nullity of the Clifford hypersurface in the fiber-squashing range of the quaternionic Berger family. Finally, for the identity map on the quaternionic Hopf--Berger spheres, we determine its Morse--index by an explicit sequence of transition parameters.

metadata.title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem
metadata.abstract: We place two disks inside the unit disk so that they touch each other and the unit circle. We then insert a disk of the largest possible radius, requiring it to touch both original disks. We show that the smallest possible sum of the three areas is $11\pi/18$, and find all equality cases. We give three solutions, using Descartes' circle theorem, inversion, and contact-point coordinates. The main difficulty is checking that the third disk is largest among all disks that fit, not only among disks touching the first two.

metadata.title: Continuous improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
metadata.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

analysisBasis.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

metadata.title: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
metadata.abstract: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative. In contrast, we prove that any smooth $\mathbb{Z}_n$-action on $K3$ for which the fixed point set has only non-isolated fixed points preserves an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class. In particular, this applies to the Fintushel-Stern-Sunukjian examples. Lastly, we classify the possible fixed point data and action on cohomology for cyclic group actions on $K3$ of prime order which preserve an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class.

metadata.title: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
metadata.abstract: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

metadata.title: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
metadata.abstract: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. metadata.title: Algebraic Vector Fields on Compact Homogeneous Spaces are 2-generated
metadata.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact, connected manifold on which a compact Lie group $K$ acts smoothly and transitively. We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on $M$, i.e., of smooth vector fields whose translates under $K$ span finite-dimensional spaces, is generated by two vector fields. For spheres, explicit generators are obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.

metadata.title: Orbifold Morse Handles II. Boundary Regions, Gluing Maps, and Surgery Cobordisms
metadata.abstract: We study four-dimensional quotient handles defined by faithful representations of finite groups in $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ and invariant splittings of indices $1$, $2$, and $3$. We identify their attaching and belt regions as oriented $3$-orbifolds described by labeled singular graphs. We determine the orbifold isotopy class of the boundary gluing map. Fix an orientation-reversing orbifold embedding of the attaching region into an oriented $3$-orbifold. Assume that the embedding induces isomorphisms on local groups. The regions, gluing class, and embedding determine the surgery. For a fixed handle and attaching image, an extension condition on the belt region characterizes diffeomorphisms of the cobordisms fixing a specified common exterior pointwise. For index-$2$ handles, this condition is the vanishing of an integer twist in the fixed boundary coordinates. We use these surgeries to construct a compact connected oriented $4$-orbifold cobordism from every closed connected oriented $3$-orbifold $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$. A finite sequence of index-$2$ orbifold handle attachments from $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$ exists if and only if $\mathcal O$ has no tetrahedral, octahedral, or icosahedral vertices. Let $v_{\mathbf T}(\mathcal O)$, $v_{\mathbf O}(\mathcal O)$, and $v_{\mathbf I}(\mathcal O)$ denote the numbers of these vertices. Among finite sequences of handle attachments of indices $1$, $2$, and $3$ from $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$, the minimum total number of index-$1$ and index-$3$ handles is $\left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf T}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil+ \left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf O}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil+ \left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf I}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil$.

metadata.title: On the volume growth assumption in the Eulerian definition of RCD spaces
metadata.abstract: We prove that every infinitesimally Hilbertian metric measure space whose reference measure is a Radon measure, and which satisfies the Sobolev-to-Lipschitz property and the weak Bochner inequality with a lower Ricci bound, has Gaussian volume growth; in particular, balls have finite measure. Hence, in the Eulerian definition of $\mathsf{RCD}(K,\infty)$ spaces, both the volume growth assumption and the finiteness of the measure of balls are redundant. metadata.title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
metadata.abstract: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations, generalising, and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

metadata.title: Almost-Global Coordinates on Matrix Manifolds
metadata.abstract: We study global coordinates on smooth manifolds outside some closed subsets of measure zero. We first give an elementary proof that every compact smooth manifold admits such coordinates, allowing the Euclidean parameter domain to be disconnected. We then study parametrizations of classical matrix groups, Stiefel manifolds, Grassmannians and real flag manifolds. For these parametrizations, we describe the inverse maps and compute the codimensions of the omitted subsets. We construct these parametrizations using Cayley transforms, graphs of linear maps and block Gaussian elimination. We also give formulas for Riemannian gradients and Haar integrals in these coordinates.

metadata.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
metadata.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

metadata.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
metadata.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I \gamma_{\Sigma_i}(K_i)^{\tilde \lambda_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}\gamma_\Gamma\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,\Sigma_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $\gamma_{\Sigma_i}$ is zero, where $\lambda_i, \tilde \lambda_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde \lambda_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $\Gamma, \Sigma_1,\cdots,\Sigma_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

metadata.title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
metadata.abstract: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. metadata.abstract: We give a global conceptual viewpoint of two constructions of Poisson structures involving $r$-matrices: the first one concerns coupling of generalized dynamical $r$-matrices with actions of quasi-triangular Lie bialgebras, the second one is given by the mixed products of Poisson spaces, which combine two Poisson actions of a quasi-triangular Lie bialgebra to create a new one. metadata.title: Symphonic Joins and Finite-Product Hopf Constructions
metadata.abstract: We study how collapse at the ends of a warped product affects symphonic joins and Hopf constructions. For a Hopf construction with a fixed angular map on a finite product of closed Riemannian manifolds, we characterize when the reduced energy has infimum zero among functions connecting the two target poles. Under linear collapse this occurs precisely when, at some end, the collapsing factors have total dimension greater than three, or have total dimension three and vanishing angular density on the collapsing block. In either case the infimum is unattained. For ellipsoidal joins with nonconstant spherical factor maps, smooth extension of a connecting symphonic join forces each factor map to be the restriction of a linear isometric embedding. We also derive the coupled equations for orthogonally split targets, establish a convexity criterion for minimizing separated joins, and construct smooth quaternionic examples with all angular factors active.

metadata.title: Rank-sensitive Hodge bounds for symphonic energy and minimizers on sheared tori
metadata.abstract: We ask how far the minimum of symphonic energy in a homotopy class can exceed the Hodge lower bound from a pulled-back two-form. For projections from a family of sheared four-tori to the flat two-torus, we compute the minimum and the gap for every smooth shear profile. The gap depends on the variance of the profile. Attainment of the projection's pullback area energy by a coclosed test depends on its oscillation. We determine exactly which variances allow two profiles with the same positive gap and different outcomes for this test, and compute the convex relaxation beyond the oscillation threshold. In arbitrary source dimension the optimized test improves the Hodge bound precisely when the harmonic representative exceeds the rank allowed for the pullback on a set of positive measure. We also prove low-degree cohomology estimates, a sharp universal degree exponent for targets detected by low-degree cup products, and an exact defect identity that forces an immersed source to be symplectic at equality.

metadata.title: Pluricanonical locally conformally almost Kähler metrics, circle-invariant $G_2$ structures, and Laplacian flows
metadata.abstract: We study explicit Hodge evolutions of pluricanonical locally conformally almost Kähler metrics and their relation to locally conformal parallel $G_2$ structures. A compact locally conformal parallel $7$-manifold with a parallel non-zero Lee form, carrying a structure-preserving free circle action of constant orbit length orthogonal to the Lee field, has a $6$-dimensional quotient which is pluricanonical with a parallel Lee form and a non-integrable almost complex structure. The fundamental forms upstairs and downstairs are Laplacian eigenforms with an explicit eigenvalue ratio. Conversely, for a fixed normalized $SU(3)$ completion, we characterize the curvature of a circle-invariant locally conformal parallel lift. The lift equations force a pluricanonical base to have parallel Lee form, even locally, and exclude strict integrable pluricanonical bases. Independently, the pluricanonical eigenform identity gives a shrinking solution of He's full Hodge equation and an immortal $d^*d$ solution contracting the Lee plane.

metadata.abstract: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-Müller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.

metadata.title: First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons
metadata.abstract: We develop a first order calculus based on the geometry of realised diameter graphs for perimeter maximisation among convex equilateral small polygons. Polygon side equalities and active diameter constraints define a linearised feasible cone and an associated equality space. We prove that an equilateral small polygon is a strict local maximiser of perimeter modulo Euclidean motions if a multiplier balance holds with strictly positive active diameter multipliers and the active equality space consists only of infinitesimal Euclidean motions. The proof uses a local Euclidean slice and a geometric limiting argument and requires neither independence of the active constraint gradients nor second order information. As an application, we combine our criterion with validated interval arithmetic to establish strict local maximality for Bingane and Audet's polygons $A_{16}$, $A_{32}$, $A_{64}$ and for reconstructions of their polygons $Z_{32}$ and $Z_{64}$. For each $n\in\{32,64\}$, the perimeter of $Z_n$ is strictly larger than that of $A_n$. Thus, strict local maximisers with different perimeters coexist in the space of convex equilateral small polygons with the same number of sides.

metadata.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampère equations in big classes
metadata.abstract: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampère equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact Kähler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.
